prompt: Stage 3-3, level 6 with 56 gold and 66 HP on a 6-loss streak you planned, with a 3-5 exit. Level 7 costs only 4 XP this round and a 2-star 2-cost bruiser sits on your bench. Your next opponent has two itemised 2-star 3-costs. Do you level and field the bruiser to try to win this one?

options.label: No. Bank, keep the streak, and level 7 at 3-5 when the passive XP has paid for it and you roll with a surplus
Yes: 4 gold for a level and a 2-star is cheap, and the fight might go either way
Roll 20 now instead: at 66 HP the streak has paid enough

explanation:
Ask whether the bigger board wins the fight. A 2-star 2-cost bruiser next to a 1-star carry does not beat two itemised 2-star 3-costs; you lose either way, about 9 HP. So the level buys nothing this round, and it is not even cheap: two rounds of passive XP give you level 7 at 3-5 for free, so the 4 gold pays for a slot used one round early on a board that loses regardless.

The real risk is winning by accident. A 6-loss streak pays 3 gold a round. One lucky win resets it; the next loss pays 0 and the one after 1, so a single win costs about 5 gold of streak on top of the 4 you spent, for 9 HP you were prepared to lose. That is the accidental loss streak.

The exit is 3-5, one loss away. You arrive near 57 HP with over 60 gold and level 7 for free, and the surplus becomes the rolldown that turns the streak into a board. Rolling now at 6, at 25% 3-cost odds with two rounds of interest still to collect, is exiting early at worse odds.
principle: Keep the streak while a bigger board would still lose; spend on the round when the board can actually win.
commonMistake: Spending 'only 4 gold' to level on a losing round, then winning one fight by accident and losing the streak bonus.
hint: Before spending anything, decide honestly whether the extra unit wins this fight, and what a single win does to the streak gold.
